properties.arch_context_note: Located in the Exmoor Devonian sandstone moorland (Somerset / North Devon), this 9 m² topographic anomaly (+0.20 m local relief, 0.099 / 5.7° mean scarp slope, nDSM 0.02 m) mimics prehistoric earthwork geometry in 1 m LiDAR but is automatically separated by the spatial/geometric filter as 'barrier=hedge'. Steep machine-graded scarps, negative-relief extraction pits, or mapped modern infrastructure distinguish it from weathered prehistoric mounds despite proximity to Deserted medieval farm, W of Bramble Combe (NHLE #1006126, 366 m NE) and Iron Age defended settlement, Furzebury Brake (NHLE #1008809, 682 m NNW).
